analysis.summary: WTC beat its own guidance EBITDA target (US$585.8m guidance vs US$558.4m reported, with the delta explained by restructuring and divestment add-backs) and delivered Underlying EBITDA of US$644.5m, up 56%, squarely above the reaffirmed guidance range. The e2open acquisition (11 months consolidated) accounts for essentially all revenue growth, with organic CargoWise growth a solid but unspectacular 8% ex-FX and acquisitions. Cash conversion was clean: operating cash flow of US$564m produced an underlying OCF conversion of 100% and free cash flow of US$410.7m, up 43%. The final dividend of 8.8cps (+14%) signals confidence but is modest relative to earnings given the priority is deleveraging from 2.7x net leverage toward <2.0x by FY28. The single biggest forward risk is e2open revenue attrition: subscription churn and professional-services run-off are ongoing, guidance assumes flat e2open revenue in FY27, and any acceleration in customer losses would undermine the margin expansion story.
analysis.full_analysis:
## Executive summary
- Revenue more than doubled to US$1,396m, but US$541m came from e2open (11 months); organic CargoWise growth was 8% ex-FX/M&A, a deceleration vs the US$82.7m existing-customer growth posted in FY25 (only US$38.5m in FY26 from existing customers).
- Underlying EBITDA of US$644.5m beat guidance; margin compressed 7pp to 46% as e2open's lower-margin (~36% underlying) business now represents ~39% of group revenue.
- Statutory NPAT fell 11% to US$178.7m because US$133.6m of net finance costs (from the acquisition debt) and US$205.1m of D&A (including US$86.8m acquired amortization) crushed reported earnings even as EBITDA rose strongly.
- Red flag: e2open recurring subscription revenue is still attriting; the company explicitly says churn will continue in FY27 and guides to flat e2open revenue.
- Working capital was a US$65.1m drag in FY26, reversing the US$22m tailwind of FY25, partly due to the new CVP commercial model transition and e2open billing cycle changes.

## Key numbers

| Metric | FY26 | FY25 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total revenue | US$1,395.9m | US$778.7m | +79% |
| CargoWise revenue | US$756.9m | US$682.2m | +11% |
| e2open revenue | US$541.2m | nil | n/m |
| Gross profit | US$1,101.8m | US$681.3m | +62% |
| Gross profit margin | 79% | 87% | -9pp |
| Reported EBITDA | US$558.4m | US$381.6m | +46% |
| Reported EBITDA margin | 40% | 49% | -9pp |
| Underlying EBITDA | US$644.5m | US$413.9m | +56% |
| Underlying EBITDA margin | 46% | 53% | -7pp |
| D&A | US$205.1m | US$90.3m | +127% |
| EBIT | US$353.3m | US$291.3m | +21% |
| Net finance costs | US$133.6m | US$3.5m | n/m |
| Statutory NPAT | US$178.7m | US$200.7m | -11% |
| Statutory basic EPS | 53.6cps | 60.4cps | -11% |
| Underlying NPAT | US$313.5m | US$243.0m | +29% |
| Underlying EPS | 94.0cps | 73.1cps | +28% |
| Operating cash flow | US$564.0m | US$436.5m | +29% |
| Underlying OCF | US$642.9m | US$441.8m | +46% |
| Free cash flow | US$410.7m | US$287.0m | +43% |
| Underlying FCF | US$489.6m | US$292.4m | +67% |
| Net debt / leverage | 2.7x | ~0.0x | n/m |
| Cash on balance sheet | US$343.5m | US$167.4m | +105% |
| Borrowings | US$2,187.4m | US$65.0m | n/m |

## Quality of earnings
- Underlying OCF conversion of 100% (down 7pp) is respectable for a year that included a transformational acquisition and a commercial model transition.
- Working capital was a US$65.1m outflow vs a US$22.0m inflow in FY25. Management attributes this to timing of commercial contract arrangements and e2open deferred revenue of US$188.6m on the balance sheet (which will unwind). This is worth monitoring in FY27.
- Capitalized development rose to US$142.5m (FY25: US$126.5m) and now includes e2open. The capitalization rate fell to 45% (FY25: 55%), and management says this will stabilize as e2open transitions to a product-led model. Ongoing scrutiny warranted.
- Restructuring costs of US$67.1m (FY25: US$1.7m) are the dominant underlying-to-reported bridge item. While real cash costs, they are excluded from underlying metrics; at US$43.1m in cash payments in FY26 they are material. These are labeled as non-recurring but WTC has run restructuring charges in multiple consecutive years.
- M&A costs were US$11.9m (FY25: US$30.6m), declining as e2open integration matures.
- Receivables jumped US$103.3m to US$198.1m; while largely e2open consolidation, DSO expansion from the CVP transition and new billing cycles bears watching.
- Development cost WIP fell 54% to US$39.2m, indicating products are being commercialized rather than sitting in pipeline, which is a positive quality signal.

## Management framing
**Rating: Mixed / Promotional**
- The deck leads with "record revenue growth" and the 79% revenue jump without immediately disclosing that ~US$541m of this is a first-time e2open consolidation, not organic growth. Organic WTG-ex-e2open growth was only 6% on a total revenue basis.
- Guidance EBITDA of US$585.8m is presented as a beat, but this metric is itself an adjusted version of reported EBITDA (adding back AI Transformation net cost and divestment loss). Management is comparing an adjusted FY26 number against an adjusted guidance number, adding a layer of obfuscation.
- The 8pp e2open EBITDA margin expansion vs FY25 pro forma is compared against unaudited pro forma figures, not audited comparatives.
- Statutory NPAT declining 11% is disclosed clearly in the table, which is credit-worthy transparency, but the headline metrics throughout the presentation are Underlying NPAT (+29%) and Underlying EBITDA (+56%), which crowd out the statutory deterioration.
- The FY27 guidance for e2open at flat revenue explicitly acknowledges ongoing subscription attrition and professional services decline, but this is buried in the assumptions text rather than flagged as a headline risk.
- AI productivity claims (90%+ code written by or assisted by AI, 45% engineering productivity gain) are compelling but presented without external verification or clear revenue attribution.

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Gross Margin | Underlying EBITDA | Underlying EBITDA Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| WTG ex. e2open | US$854.8m (+10% on FY25) | 87% | US$451.2m | 53% (flat) |
| e2open | US$541.2m (11 months) | 67% | US$197.4m | 36% |
| Unallocated | nil | n/a | -US$4.0m | n/a |
| Group | US$1,395.9m | 79% | US$644.5m | 46% |

- WTG ex. e2open margin held flat at 53% despite higher legal/compliance/advisory costs, offset by restructuring savings. This is the core business behaving well.
- e2open at 36% underlying EBITDA margin is structurally dilutive to the legacy ~53% group margin and will remain so until deeper integration and product-led transformation are completed.
- CargoWise organic revenue growth of 8% (ex-FX, ex-M&A) decelerated from prior years; existing customer growth of US$38.5m compares unfavorably to US$82.7m in FY25, reflecting the transition friction from the new CargoWise Value Pack (CVP) commercial model launched December 2025.
- Non-CargoWise revenue fell 8% organically as expected legacy wind-down continues.

## Balance sheet
- Net leverage of 2.7x at 30 June 2026; the company targets ~2.2x by end of FY27 and <2.0x by FY28.
- Borrowings of US$2.19b against a US$3.0b unsecured facility (syndicate of 25+ banks). US$343.5m cash gives net debt of approximately US$1.84b.
- Total assets nearly doubled to US$4.87b, driven by US$1.4b goodwill and US$0.9b acquired intangible assets from e2open.
- Acquired intangibles of US$864.4m will amortize at a run-rate of ~US$86-100m+ per annum, permanently suppressing statutory NPAT.
- Deferred revenue of US$188.6m on e2open's balance sheet represents a future revenue headwind as shorter billing cycles are adopted.
- No covenant breach indicators disclosed; no refinancing risk flagged given a multi-bank syndicated facility.
- Net assets increased to US$1,942.4m from US$1,703.9m.

## Dividend and capital allocation
- Final ordinary dividend of 8.8cps AUD, up 14% on FY25. This is the only dividend disclosed (no interim referenced in this presentation, likely due to the presentation covering the full year result).
- No special dividend; capital allocation priority is clearly debt reduction.
- US$153.3m of capex invested primarily in product development and data center capacity in FY26.
- Share capital increased by US$87.7m to fund employee equity programs, a steady dilution that investors should track against EPS growth.
- The dividend payout relative to underlying EPS is modest, consistent with a company prioritizing deleveraging over distributions.

## Guidance and outlook
- FY27 Revenue guidance: US$1.48b-US$1.54b (+6% to +10% vs FY26).
- FY27 Underlying EBITDA guidance: US$725m-US$780m (+12% to +21% vs FY26).
- FY27 Underlying EBITDA margin guidance: 49%-51% (implying 3-5pp expansion from FY26's 46%).
- CargoWise guided at ~12-20% growth; e2open guided flat.
- The guidance range is wide and management explicitly states the upper end requires accelerated CVP adoption and AI monetization, both customer-dependent.
- 1H/2H skew of 45/55 for CargoWise revenue is flagged, meaning 2H FY27 is load-bearing for hitting guidance.
- The effective tax rate assumed at 23-27% (FY26 underlying ETR was 24.0%, statutory ETR was 19.3% due to US$42.9m tax on US$221.6m PBT).
- No explicit revenue synergy guidance for e2open was provided; guidance assumes flat e2open revenue only.

## Positives
- Underlying EBITDA of US$644.5m beat guidance by approximately US$58.7m (vs the US$585.8m guidance EBITDA benchmark).
- Free cash flow of US$410.7m (+43%) and underlying FCF of US$489.6m (+67%) demonstrate the business generates genuine cash.
- e2open cost synergies of US$64m annualized run-rate savings achieved in FY26, ahead of the FY27 US$50m target, with 8pp e2open EBITDA margin expansion from FY25 pro forma.
- Total group annualized run-rate savings of ~US$115m from restructuring programs.
- CargoWise customer attrition remains below 1% for the 14th consecutive year; 90%+ of customer cohorts grew revenue in FY26.
- 61 LGFF global rollouts (49 in production, 12 contracted), up from 55 at June 2025, with 4 new contracts signed post-year-end.
- 95%+ of CargoWise customers now on CVP commercial model, enabling the shift to value-based pricing.
- AI productivity gains are concrete and measurable: 45% engineering productivity increase, 22% faster customer service ticket resolution, reducing ~1,200 roles for US$34m run-rate savings.
- Deleveraging trajectory is ahead of prior targets (2.7x vs ~3.0x guided; <2.0x FY28 target vs prior ~2.5x).

## Negatives / red flags
- Statutory NPAT fell 11% to US$178.7m; the gap between underlying (US$313.5m) and statutory (US$178.7m) is US$134.8m, driven by US$81.1m acquired amortization net of tax, US$51.2m restructuring net of tax, and US$7.2m divestment loss. This is a structurally large and recurring adjustment pool.
- Net leverage of 2.7x is elevated; US$133.6m in net finance costs is now a permanent P&L burden that did not exist in FY25.
- e2open revenue attrition is ongoing and guided to continue in FY27. e2open's subscription revenue is described as experiencing "minor continued attrition" and professional services will decline further. At US$541m for 11 months, e2open flat in FY27 means any incremental attrition would require CargoWise to grow faster than guided to compensate.
- Existing CargoWise customer growth decelerated sharply: US$38.5m in FY26 vs US$82.7m in FY25, likely reflecting CVP transition disruption. This must recover for the upper end of FY27 guidance to be achievable.
- Underlying EBITDA margin compressed 7pp to 46% despite significant cost-out. The group has structurally lower margin than pre-acquisition and returning to 50%+ requires both e2open improvement and CargoWise re-acceleration.
- Restructuring costs of US$67.1m in FY26 (vs US$1.7m in FY25) are material; these are classified as non-recurring but WTC has a history of ongoing restructuring charges.
- Working capital outflow of US$65.1m represents a real cash drag and may reflect timing issues that could persist as e2open billing transitions occur.
- Management is still on an interim CFO; governance and leadership stability remain a background concern.
- Gross margin compressed 9pp to 79% due to e2open's structurally lower 67% gross margin. This will not recover to 87% without deep e2open transformation.

## Bottom line
**Bull case:** e2open cost synergies materialize faster than guided, CargoWise CVP adoption re-accelerates existing customer revenue growth back toward FY25 levels, AI monetization begins to contribute incremental revenue by 2H FY27, and the group hits the upper end of guidance (US$1.54b revenue, US$780m Underlying EBITDA, 51% margin). At that margin with continued deleveraging and CargoWise's near-monopoly positioning in global freight forwarding software, the business is deeply attractive.

**Bear case:** e2open subscription attrition accelerates beyond guidance assumptions, CVP adoption stalls or creates more churn than expected in 2H, AI-led pricing uplift is delayed, and the company delivers the lower end of guidance (US$1.48b revenue, US$725m EBITDA, 49% margin). With 2.7x leverage and US$133m annual interest burden, any miss on EBITDA flows directly to a deteriorating debt position.

**What would change the view:** Quarterly or half-year data showing e2open ARR stabilizing or growing; evidence of CargoWise existing-customer revenue growth returning above US$60m in 1H FY27; and meaningful AI-agent revenue contribution in any disclosed metric would all be positively decisive. Conversely, e2open attrition accelerating or CargoWise CVP-related churn materializing would be clear negative triggers.
